_eval_note: The behaviour-contract rows added 2026-10-01 (road-to-behavior-vocabulary-and-runner-truth step 1.1) have NOT been through a live `skill_trigger_eval` pass — that runner needs an on-disk key and a controlling-terminal confirmation, neither of which an execution session clears. `last_eval` therefore still dates the last pass that actually ran and is deliberately not bumped: the rows are corpus, not a measurement. THESE ROWS ARE EXPECTED TO FAIL A LIVE PASS TODAY, and saying so is the point of this note rather than a hedge. The production routing condition is this skill's frontmatter `description`, which step 1.1 deliberately did not touch and which carries none of this vocabulary; the corpus is not itself a routing surface. So the exemplars record the behaviour the suite SHOULD have, not behaviour it has — a specification, red until the description changes or a router reads bodies. Whoever next runs a live pass should expect these rows red and read that as the known gap, not as a regression. Annotation, never input — nothing reads it at run time, hence the underscore prefix.
description: 15 exemplars + 9 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Exemplars cover DE + EN phrasings for pre-write test-case enumeration (what to test, edge cases, coverage breadth) and — added 2026-10-01 — for the behaviour-contract discriminator at SKILL.md § 'Does this change owe an executable behavior contract?': gherkin, BDD, cucumber, behat, given-when-then, feature file, executable specification, specification by example, living documentation, Szenarien, Akzeptanzkriterien. Near-misses cover the adjacent skills (testing-anti-patterns, judge-test-coverage, systematic-debugging, pest-testing, playwright-testing) and the four the discriminator's own no-cases protect — a refactor with no observable change, scenario-per-unit-case, a selector-and-click step script, and an internal invariant with no external vocabulary. Counterexamples guard the two directions the vocabulary over-claims: adopting a runner the repository does not have, and an unrelated use of the word 'test'.

queries.q: what should we test here — I don't want happy-path-only coverage
enumerate the edge cases for this endpoint before we write the tests
welche Testfälle brauchen wir für dieses Feature — auch Grenzfälle und Fehlerpfade?
build a case matrix for this behavior — happy, boundary, error, abuse
ask a subagent what else we could test so coverage is broad
does this change owe a Gherkin feature file, or are unit cases enough?
queries.note: the behaviour-contract discriminator itself — the yes/no question SKILL.md § 'Does this change owe an executable behavior contract?' answers
